newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Boots to open in Japan, Thailand, Netherlands.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Boots to open in Japan, Thailand, Netherlands.

text.p: Chemist and retailer Boots, one of the best known names on British shopping streets, said on Thursday it is to open up stores in Thailand, the Netherlands and Japan over the next 18 months.
The group, which said in June it was investigating overseas expansion, will invest 30 million pounds ($47 million) in the trial stores, which it will manage with local partners.

Boots deputy chairman and chief executive Lord Blyth and William Heinecke of the Minor Group have signed an agreement in Bangkok to set up a joint venture and open five shops in Thailand by the summer of 1997. Four of the shops would be located in Bangkok and one in Pattaya.
Three pilot stores will also open in the Netherlands next summer after the company signed a deal with Dutch healthcare provider EVA to supply in-store pharmacy services.
Boots said it would make a further announcement shortly about plans for a trial in Japan.
Lord Blyth said Boots had chosen the three countries after an "exhaustive review."

"The purpose of opening these pilot stores is to carry out a thorough evaluation of the commercial opportunities and operational issues before considering the scope for further investment in these countries or elsewhere," he said in a statement.
Boots said the health and beauty market in Thailand is expected to double in real terms over the next 10 years driven mainly by the growing middle class urban population.

The stores, which will closely resemble Boots The Chemists stores in appearance and layout, will have a pharmacy handling prescription and over-the-counter medicines and stock a wide range of fragrances, cosmetics and toiletries, including major Boots brands such as No7 cosmetics and Natural Collection toiletries.

Boots partner in Thailand Minor Group is a holding company with substantial investments in publicly quoted companies in food manufacture and retailing, fashion and cosmetics marketing and hotel and retail property management.
In the Netherlands the pilot stores will look similar to Boots health and beauty stores in Britain and carry similar ranges to the outlets in Thailand.

Boots joins a growing list of British retailers who are expanding overseas. Marks & Spencer now has stores in France, Spain, the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany and franchises in many more countries. Fashion group Next has international franchises and J. Sainsbury, the supermarket group, owns stores in the United States.
